You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like May 2022.

- **Rates:** The fed funds rate is 0.83%, which fits the May 2022 level after the March and May hikes. The 10-year yield is 2.74% and the 2-year is 2.47%.
- **Inflation and labor:** Headline CPI at 8.22% matches the April 2022 reading (8.3%) and fits a figure published in May. Core CPI at 6.13% and unemployment at 3.6% fit as well.
- **Markets:** US large-cap equity is up only 0.2% over the month, after sitting near its lows in mid-May. The 12-month return of -0.3% is consistent with that.
- **Dollar:** The trade-weighted dollar is up 6.9% year over year, which fits.

The 10-year at 2.74% is a little low for the end of May, when it was about 2.85%. The 3-month change in the policy rate of +0.75 matches a window from March through May. That is consistent with May.
